correctness.rationale: For a cross-part move, the source and target are respectively full just before and after the jump. The moving player's prior utility is the marginal term q_i,c(n_i,c); its successor utility is q_j,c(n_j,c+1), exactly the two potential terms lost and gained. Within-part jumps are utility- and count-neutral. The finite number of count matrices gives termination and the stated path bound. In the explicit K_{3,3} two-vacancy cycle, each rational payoff gain is positive (2/3 to 1, then 0 to 2/3, repeated), and the full profile returns. Standard-library exact-rational computations verify all 2,556 directed test transitions and the four state changes. The proof, not bounded tests, establishes the universal theorem.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The originating paper exhibits failures on some graphs and proves equilibria for particular families; those claims do not imply exact potentials for every complete multipartite graph and arbitrary type/part utility. The modified-game utility is not the self-inclusive fraction here. Resource choice with capacity/tolerance does not impose one-to-one vertex occupancy and a single vacancy. An earlier complete-bipartite diversity potential concerns a different monotone other-type payoff and does not imply nonlinear self-inclusive potential.

originality.rationale: The originating 2023 paper studies the self-inclusive single-peaked rule and cycles or existence conditions in other graph classes but does not state the classwide complete-multipartite exact potential and linear bipartite bound found here. The 2020 modified-game paper normalizes the different other-agent neighbor fraction. The 2023 homophilic resource-selection paper permits a different allocation/action geometry. An accessible earlier complete-bipartite diversity potential addresses other-type fractions among occupied neighbors, not the present nonlinear self-inclusive utility. The new two-vacancy cycle specifically marks the failure of this universal one-vacancy guarantee. Residual risk: a Rosenthal-like reduction or unindexed literature may contain an equivalent structural result.
residual_risks: The marginal potential is structurally akin to classical congestion-game potentials; a general theorem yielding this specific normalization may exist under another name.
Unindexed publications, later extensions to the originating game, or alternative formulations may cover some or all claims.

value.rationale: Single-peaked/nonmonotone jump Schelling games can exhibit improving cycles even on regular host graphs, so an entire graph-family finite-improvement guarantee is a meaningful structural gap. The potential handles arbitrary real nonlinear type/part utilities, gives finite and polynomial count-state bounds (linear for bipartite two-color cases), and identifies a strict sharp boundary at two vacancies via a short cycle. The result is not an arbitrary finite census or trivial model-renaming. Limitations: no global dynamics under neutral moves and no assertion for multiple-vacancy general families.
